cause_quote: The new Linux copier called `await flush()` whenever `batch.length === 128`, and `flush()` called `childProcess.spawn("cp", ...)` from the Gateway's worker thread for every batch.
user_saw: New managed worktrees took tens of seconds longer to become ready when a large Linux Gateway copied a large dependency tree.
summary: The fix starts one small helper per Linux provisioning operation to launch all GNU cp batches and records bounded copy timings in the preparation log.
reasoning: The parent of #196298 used a portable per-file copier, and #196298 introduced the batched Linux path with one GNU cp spawn per batch from a thread in the Gateway process. The intervening #196390 added an authority check after the child settled, leaving the spawn loop in place. The fix PR's measurements traced the slowdown to repeated spawns from a large process even while copy-on-write remained active.
